transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've been asked to restore a worn 1920s community cookbook. It has a detached cover and several loose pages. Before I decide whether to accept the commission and set the final terms, I'd like to hear from everyone present — please state any terms, offers, or material constraints you know of. That way we can get everything on the table before I make my decision.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: My barter proposal is this: Inez reattaches the cover, resews the loose sections, and makes a simple cloth spine. In exchange, I'll provide twelve archival linen sheets plus $40. I'd bring the book Tuesday at 18:00 and collect it Saturday at 16:00.

transcript.text: I inspected this cookbook for a local archivist, who confirmed that its brittle acidic pages require wheat-starch paste and Japanese tissue for the loose-page repairs. Ordinary PVA glue should not be used. I'd ask that this material constraint be included in the final terms if the commission is accepted.
